sections.content: How many people stayed in Evesham after gaining qualifications?

Evesham is a medium-sized town in the West Midlands. Evesham does not have its own university.

Evesham has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Evesham ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,120 state-school pupils from Evesham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 315 (28%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 410 (37%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Evesham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Evesham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Evesham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Evesham move to?

Of Evesham's graduates, 135 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Evesham's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 125 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those qualified non-graduates (40%) were living fairly locally, in the Evesham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Evesham's GCSE cohort:

  • 105 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the South West
  • 45 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 29% of graduates and 30% of qualified non-graduates living in Evesham had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 245 graduates and 395 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Evesham. This is compared with the 315 graduates and 410 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 71% of the graduates had also lived in Evesham as GCSE pupils, while 29% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Evesham in 2018 to 2019, 71% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 30% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
